findings.summary: The store's latest snapshot of the project is not the one this working copy came from (another copy was offloaded since, or the project is conflicted); nothing local is deleted
A catalog event file is not JSON, does not match its schema, is named for another id, or has a type this version does not know; it is left out of the fold and never changed
The catalog names a snapshot of the project it does not hold (a partial mirror), so its head is unknown; sync the store or run plainport doctor
The person answering the prompts cancelled; nothing was written
No registered command has this name; the message suggests the closest one
A config file does not parse or does not match its schema, and there is no last good copy to keep
A config file broke since it was last loaded; its last good contents stay in effect
Another process holds managed.toml.lock
HOME is unset or not an absolute path, so plainport cannot find its config and state
The config file named by --config or PLAINPORT_CONFIG does not exist
config.toml sets this already and wins over managed.toml, so plainport will not write a copy it would shadow; edit config.toml
A write would rewrite config.toml, which plainport never does
managed.toml or device.json could not be written; the old file is intact
A value crossing an edge did not match its schema
A package folder holds lockfiles of more than one package manager and no packageManager field says which to use
A package folder has no lockfile for its package manager, so onload would resolve fresh dependency versions
device.json, this device's identity, is unreadable; plainport never replaces it
This device has no identity yet; plainport init creates it
A running container bind-mounts the project folder or a folder inside it; offloading would pull files from under it
A file is an iCloud or Dropbox placeholder (dataless): reading it triggers a download or fails
A symlink points outside the project; the link is stored, its target is not
plainport cannot read some files or folders in the project, so a snapshot would be incomplete
The project folder is on another volume than the folder it would be moved aside into, so release could not rename it in one step
A file or folder an operation keeps for itself (its journal, lock, trash or stub) could not be read, written or moved: permissions, a full disk, an I/O error
A git command plainport runs to read the repository's state failed; the message is git's
A rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert or bisect is in progress; it restores exactly as it is
The folder is a linked git worktree or submodule: its .git is only a pointer to a repository elsewhere
The repository's index.lock exists: a git process is running or crashed
Repositories inside the project (nested clones and submodules) travel as plain files, their own .git included
Commits or stashes exist only in this copy of the repository, so the snapshot becomes their only copy
requirePushed is set, and commits, branches or stashes exist only in this copy of the repository; push them first
Linked worktrees of this repository live outside the folder; offloading would orphan them
A bug: an exception escaped a command; the message names it
An earlier operation on this project was interrupted and its journal is still open; plainport recover finishes or rolls it back
Something other than this project's stub is at <project>.plainport, where the stub would go; plainport never overwrites it
The approved plan is more than an hour old; plan again with --dry-run

The project folder changed after its offload was committed (found by offload right before the rename, or by recover): the snapshot is the head, the folder is kept with its edits and no stub is written, and the next offload builds on the snapshot (D51, D52)
A signal (Ctrl-C, a closed terminal) stopped the operation at a safe point before it changed anything local
No saved plan has this id on this device
The folder changed since the plan was made (its fingerprint differs), or the plan is for another project; a fresh plan is saved
Another process has its working directory inside the project folder
The shell or agent that started plainport has its working directory inside the project folder
A process holds files open inside the project folder (an editor, a dev server, an agent)
A child process was cancelled; its whole process group was stopped
A child process printed nothing for its idle deadline; its whole process group was stopped
A child process exited, but its stdout, parsed as data, cannot be taken as whole: something outside its process group kept it open, reading it failed, or processes it left in its group were stopped
A child process printed more on stdout than its caller's capture limit; it was stopped rather than read in part
A child process could not be started: the program or its working folder is missing or not usable
A child process ran past its overall deadline; its whole process group was stopped
A project name matches more than one project; the message lists every candidate address
Another plainport process holds this project's lock
No project matches the name, address or path
registry.json, this device's project registry, is unreadable; plainport never overwrites it
Another process holds registry.json.lock
registry.json exists but plainport may not read it; the file is left as it is
restic exited with a fatal error (exit code 1, or one plainport does not map); the message is restic's
restic was interrupted (exit code 130) before it finished
Another restic process holds a lock on the store's repository (restic exit code 11)
restic's JSON output did not match what this restic version is known to print
A restic repository already exists where a new one was to be created
No restic repository exists at the store's location (restic exit code 10)
The store's repository has no snapshot with this id
Too many symlinks in a snapshot have names or targets that restic's listing cannot place in one pass (line breaks, ' -> '); the message lists them
restic could not read some files (restic exit code 3); the snapshot is incomplete and counts as failed, never as a partial success
The restic binary found is not the version this plainport pins and was tested with
The store's password does not open its restic repository (restic exit code 12)
A confirm-class command ran without --yes or an approved --plan
config.toml and managed.toml both define a root; config.toml wins key by key, so edit it there
A root with this key already exists
The folder is outside every root; file it with --root and --as, or add a root that holds it
No root has this key
plainport cannot write to the root's folder
Two roots on this device overlap or resolve to the same real path; every project belongs to one root
The root's folder on this device does not exist or is not a folder; --create makes it
The root is inside an iCloud Drive or Dropbox folder, whose sync clients fight with node_modules and half-written files
The root has no folder on this device; plainport root bind gives it one
A read or write in the store failed (permissions, a full disk, an I/O error); the message names the key and the error
The store at this path is not the one this device knows (its meta/v1/store.json names another id, or none): a re-pointed path, another disk or a restored copy; nothing is synced
A create-only write found the key already there; the existing value is left as it was
The store has no identity this device recorded (plainport init sets a store up: its store.json, its restic repository)
The store already holds another root's snapshots; one restic repository serves one root (ADR-0010, D48)
The store's repository password could not be read from its secret reference (env: or file: in M1)
init recorded the store but could not set it up yet (its disk is not mounted); plainport init sets it up once it is reachable
The store's folder is missing or is not a folder: a disk that is not mounted, or a path that moved
This build cannot use the store's kind yet; M1 supports local stores (an external disk or a local folder)
A .plainport stub file does not match the stub schema
--dry-run was given to a command that has no preview
The arguments or options do not match the command's declared arguments
Paths a plugin or strip.extra proposed stay in the snapshot: git tracks them, strip.keep or strip.never protects them, they hold a repository, or dependencies are kept
Files in the project changed while the snapshot was being made, again after one retry; nothing local was deleted
The snapshot's listing does not match the scan of the folder (entries, types, sizes, modes or link targets); nothing local was deleted
A bundled binary (restic or rclone) was not found
